translation_notes: prefixes: OWL->owl, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs, SKOS->skos, XSD->xsd

The extracted function relies on a module-private _safe_local() and on `from .core import PropertyType`, neither resolvable outside the package; added shim.py with faithful copies (same regex-based slugification, same PropertyType members) so both versions run, and rewired the relative import to `from shim import PropertyType`.

Every g.add((s, p, o)) becomes +{ {s} {p} {o} } under one `@graph g` set right after g is created (g is never reassigned). Two places in the original issue two consecutive .add() calls on the very same subject (class -> rdf:type + rdfs:label; property -> rdf:type + domain + range); those became one +{ s p1 o1 ; p2 o2 ; p3 o3 } rather than three separate +{ } islands, since it is exactly the same graph write with no reordering.

The region never exposes its Graph: it serialises it straight to a file and returns a Path, so comparing the two returned Path values (rdfeval.harness.run_pair's default entry-mode comparison) would prove nothing. driver.py therefore calls both entry points directly, reads the two Turtle files back, and checks isomorphism itself — the fixture Ontology instance covers a node with same_as, one with a broader parent, one plain node, properties of several PropertyType values, and a relationship with/without same_as.

Credit correction (2026-11-02, corpus/403 defect 3): dropped `@prefix` for `rdf:`, declared by the mechanical draft but never used as a term in the translated region (and not among the bindings the original sets on its graph); `rdfeval check` stays OK.

repair.driver: Le pilote sérialise désormais deux ontologies (nominale, et sans description) : la nominale gagne un parent `broader` absent de `ontology.nodes`, des propriétés FLOAT et BOOLEAN, et des propriétés DATE, POINT et LIST (membres du vrai PropertyType que xsd_for ne mappe pas, donc le repli XSD.string). Le shim reçoit les trois membres DATE, POINT, LIST du vrai PropertyType (src/seocho/ontology/core.py:65-73).
repair.remaining: Le drapeau wrong-construction (7 `{Literal(x)}` remplaçables par `{x}`) n'est pas traité : c'est un jugement.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the loop's class IRI expression is `_cls_iri(label)`, the helper that already computes it for parents (a node value that is None, outside the Dict[str, NodeDef] contract, would now fail on `.description` instead of `.same_as`; the exception propagates before serialize either way); `URIRef(ns + _safe_local(x))` becomes `ns[_safe_local(x)]` (Namespace.term builds the same URIRef); `ns_str.endswith('/') or ns_str.endswith('#')` becomes `endswith(('/', '#'))` and `ns_str = ns_str + '/'` becomes `+=`; consecutive adds on one subject become `g += [...]`; the alias loops and the guarded subclass loop become comprehensions. The try/except ImportError, the `if parent in ontology.nodes` guard and every description guard are kept.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `+{ }` with `;` for the same groups, plain loops with `+{ }` where Python has comprehensions, bare interpolations `{label}`, `{alias}` and `{x.description}` in place of Literal(x) (descriptions are guarded truthy, labels and aliases are str; a None alias would raise where Literal(None) gives 'None'), `f<{...same_as}>` for URIRef, `xsd:string` for the xsd_for default; `ns[...]` stays Python (ns is computed at run time, no @prefix can hold it).
No exception to the symmetry. The rdflib import inside the try keeps only what optimized.ldpy still reads (rdflib, Namespace, OWL, RDFS, SKOS); the ImportError guard and its message are unchanged.

Considered and rejected, an ldpy finding: `@graph as g` would replace `g = rdflib.Graph()`, the three owl/rdfs/skos binds and `@graph g` (byte-identical Turtle on the driver's calls), but the graph it creates carries the runtime's CACHED NamespaceManager (runtime._nm_for), shared by every graph created under the same prefixes; the region's `g.bind('priv', ns)` then mutates that shared manager, and a second call with another namespace serialises `@prefix priv1:` instead of `priv:` (reproduced). `@graph g` on a graph the code creates (runtime.designate binds into the graph's own manager) has no such leak, so it is kept.
The driver resolves its two files through harness._redirected and emits through harness._emit: rdfeval check proves every artefact.
